transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

My whole sense of worth feels tied up in what I weigh and how my body looks, and it’s taking over my life. My spouse got really worried because my mood and self-esteem seem to completely hinge on the scale, which finally made me realize I need help. It's gotten to the point where this obsession is overshadowing my enjoyment of both work and home.
Do you ever find yourself eating an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time, and if so, do you engage in any behaviors like vomiting or excessive exercise to make up for it?

Yes, after stressful shifts I'll lose control and plow through huge amounts of food—like half a pizza, cereal, and snacks in under an hour—feeling like I can't stop. Then, out of panic, I'll make myself throw up or take extra laxatives to "fix" it so it doesn't show on the scale the next morning. This has been happening at least once a week, and it's something I feel really ashamed of.
Would you describe your current body weight as being significantly lower than what is considered healthy for your height and age?

No, my weight isn't low at all—it's actually right in the normal range because I go to such extremes to keep it from changing. But even though the scale says I'm normal, I am still completely obsessed with that number and absolutely terrified of gaining weight.
Beyond your concerns about weight and eating, have you been experiencing a persistent low mood, loss of interest in activities, or fatigue that occurs even when you aren't focused on your body image?

I haven't really experienced a persistent low mood or lost interest in things independent of my body image and eating struggles. Any fatigue or irritability I feel seems directly tied to purging, constantly worrying about food, or how bad I feel about my body on a given day.
To better understand your patterns, how many times per week, on average, would you say you experience these episodes of eating a large amount of food followed by purging?

For the past few months, it has been a weekly cycle where I binge and purge at least once a week. If work is especially stressful, it can happen more frequently, sometimes multiple times in a single week.
